summary: whether a mean squared displacement is in its diffusive regime, by the exponent of its power law over windows of consecutive lags against a tolerance it is handed, and from which lag on

inputs.name: lags
inputs.meaning: the lag times, positive and rising, in one unit

inputs.name: msd
inputs.meaning: the mean squared displacement at each lag, positive, in one unit

inputs.name: window
inputs.meaning: how many consecutive lags each exponent is fitted over, two or more

inputs.name: tolerance
inputs.meaning: the largest distance of the exponent from one that counts as diffusive; null when none is chosen

outputs.name: state
outputs.meaning: diffusive | not_diffusive | undecided, over the last window

outputs.name: exponent
outputs.meaning: the exponent fitted over the last window

outputs.name: diffusive_from
outputs.meaning: the first lag of the earliest window from which every window is diffusive, in the lags' unit; null when none is, or without a tolerance

validity: a mean squared displacement averaged well enough that its windows are not dominated by noise; the long lags of one run carry fewer independent samples

source.citation: F. A. Oliveira, R. M. S. Ferreira, L. C. Lapas, M. H. Vainstein, Anomalous Diffusion: A Basic Mechanism for the Evolution of Inhomogeneous Systems, Front. Einstein, On the movement of small particles suspended in stationary liquids required by the molecular-kinetic theory of heat, Ann. Phys. 17 (1905) 549; read in the English translation of A. D. Cowper, in Investigations on the Theory of the Brownian Movement, ed. R. Fürth (Dover, 1956) (read 2026-11-17, https://archive.org/stream/brownian-motion-einstein/Brownian-Motion-Einstein_djvu.txt; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261117-einstein-1905-brownian-movement); NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Section 4.4.3.1 Least Squares (read 2026-11-17, https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmd/section4/pmd431.htm; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261117-nist-sematech-least-squares)
source.locus: Sec. 2.1, Eq. (18): at long times the mean square displacement goes as t^alpha; alpha = 1 normal, below subdiffusion, above superdiffusion; Sec. 1.1, Eq. (1): normal diffusion, 2dDt; Secs. 4 and 5: the mean squared displacement along one coordinate is 2Dt; Sec. 4.4.3.1: the exponent of each window is the least-squares slope of the logarithm of the msd on the logarithm of the lag

note: v1 with its source changed from encyclopedia pages to the review, the original paper and a statistics handbook, found by search; the code and the cases are v1's. No value of the sources stands behind the worked cases: each is worked by hand in its worked field, on lags that double so that each exponent is a logarithm of base two.
